correctness.rationale: For the exact \(P(9)\) Hasse poset, fully exhaustive enumeration of all 12,575 isotone selfmaps and their comparability components gives one null component of size 12,573 and two isolated base automorphisms, with a cross-check of 232,727 selfmaps of \(P(9)\oplus D_2\) in components 232,723/1/1/1/1. \(D_2\) has two automorphisms and only constant nonautomorphism selfmaps. The cap lemma reconstructs each case: selfmaps with apex-valued base images, nonautomorphic base restrictions, or constant new-apex images are null; the remaining pairs of base automorphisms and nonconstant apex transformations are isolated. Both pointwise comparison directions are checked. Composition is exact, with a zero for constant apex composites, giving the monoid law for every \(m\ge2\) independently of finite enumeration. The primary paper directly establishes the two LS-category triples; \(H_1(B_m;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^{m-1}\) follows from the graph \(K_{2,m}\). No finite experiment is extrapolated to infinity.

value.rationale: The full endomorphism monoid [Y,Y] is a natural algebraic invariant of the homotopy category. The result constructs for every \(m\ge2\) an explicit composition-preserving isomorphism between the monoids of two connected finite spaces whose weak categories differ (1 versus 2) and whose first-homology ranks differ (zero versus \(m-1\)), even while their stable and ordinary categories agree. The unbounded weak-homology separation makes the phenomenon structural and non-arbitrary. The general cap lemma exposes why the invariant loses exactly the base homotopy information and provides a reusable method. Matching counts alone would not establish this consequence.
